entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Publius Valerius Laevinus was a prominent Roman consul in 280 BC, marking a pivotal moment in the Pyrrhic War against Pyrrhus of Epirus.


As a patrician, Laevinus played a key role in shaping the fate of southern Italy, demonstrating the enduring influence of Roman politics on the region. His leadership and strategic decisions would have lasting consequences for the region and its inhabitants.


The Pyrrhic War, in which Laevinus was instrumental, was a defining moment in the history of the Mediterranean, showcasing the military prowess and diplomatic acumen of the Roman Republic.


Laevinus's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his actions and decisions contributed to the evolution of Roman power and influence in the region, leaving a lasting impact on the course of Western history.


The Pyrrhic War, with Laevinus at its forefront, was a turning point in the struggle for dominance in the Mediterranean, with far-reaching consequences for the balance of power in the ancient world.
